meta.title: Echo-Node: Voice Agent Reconstruction
meta.subtitle: Recovering the 3-layer split-stack with live-voice providers and production observability
meta.thesis: The Echo-Node voice agent must be rebuilt from its monolithic Python script into a proper 3-layer split-stack (web frontend / gateway / audio worker) with interchangeable providers, Google Gemini Live and OpenAI Realtime voice-in/voice-out, and a live monitoring dashboard showing per-turn latency, per-provider breakdowns, and interrupt metrics.
meta.audience: Cheta (project owner), AI coding agents building the implementation.

proposals.title: Replace monolithic assistant_v2.py with gateway-mediated architecture
proposals.summary: Refactor the existing Python worker into a standalone WS-connected process and build the Bun+Hono gateway. The worker becomes one of many interchangeable components.

proposals.title: Implement Gemini Multimodal Live as phase-1 provider
proposals.summary: Before building the full web frontend, implement a Gemini Live CLI mode that proves the low-latency path works, then wrap it in the provider system.

proposals.title: Build live latency dashboard before web frontend
proposals.summary: The monitoring dashboard should work in the terminal first (Textual), then be embedded in the web UI. This gives immediate observability without waiting for the full SPA.

proposals.title: Keep legacy local pipeline as fallback
proposals.summary: The existing STT→LLM→TTS local pipeline should remain functional as a `--voice` or offline mode. It tests slower but works without cloud.

proposals.title: Use Bun as the primary runtime, not Python
proposals.summary: The gateway and all live-voice provider integrations should be in TypeScript on Bun. Python is reserved for local ML inference only. This gives us WebSocket-native concurrency and a single language for the control plane.

proposals.title: Validate and document build order: CLI → TUI → Web
proposals.summary: The implementation follows the proven developer-tool pattern: CLI first (proves core logic + env var config), then TUI (richer terminal interaction), then Web (full visual frontend). Each layer is a thin wrapper over the previous, ensuring feature parity at every stage. Grounded in the history of Git, Docker, kubectl, VS Code, and Redis — all of which followed this progression.

modelReplies.prompt: Should the legacy local pipeline be kept indefinitely or deprecated after live-voice providers work?
modelReplies.context: P-004 approves keeping it, but the maintenance cost is ongoing.

decision.rationale: Keep indefinitely for A/B testing. The legacy pipeline serves as the control group when comparing live-voice providers against local STT→LLM→TTS. Essential for latency and quality benchmarking.

options.label: Keep indefinitely
options.text: Maintain as offline fallback for A/B testing against live-voice providers.

options.label: Deprecate after Phase 5
options.text: Remove after Gemini Live and OpenAI Realtime are stable. Simplify codebase.

options.label: Keep but don't actively maintain
options.text: Fix if it breaks but don't invest more.

modelReplies.prompt: Which frontend should be built first — web or TUI?
modelReplies.context: Both have value. Validated build order via established developer-tool history: CLI → TUI → Web is the proven pattern (Git, Docker, kubectl, VS Code).

decision.rationale: CLI first proves the core logic and env-var config. TUI builds on that with keyboard-driven interaction. Web wraps everything in rich visuals. Each layer is a thin wrapper over the previous, enforcing feature parity at every stage.

options.label: CLI → TUI → Web
options.text: Proven pattern. CLI forces clean API design. TUI adds interactivity. Web adds rich visuals. Feature parity enforced at each layer.

options.label: Web first
options.text: Richer avatar, waveform, and settings. Matches the original design spec.

options.label: Both in parallel
options.text: Split work across agents. Gateway serves both.

modelReplies.prompt: Gate mechanism audit: the original gate was self-policed (agent wrote + ran the check). Should we install an external gate mechanism?
modelReplies.context: The gate-check.sh script was agent-written and agent-run. Real gates require external enforcement: a CI pipeline, a pre-commit hook, or a second agent running independent verification.

options.label: Install GitHub Actions CI
options.text: Create a .github/workflows/check.yml that runs gate-check.sh on every push. External to any agent.

options.label: Install pre-commit hook
options.text: Add a pre-commit hook that runs gate-check.sh and rejects commits that fail. Enforced by git, outside agent control.

options.label: Second-agent verification
options.text: Before marking any phase complete, dispatch a second agent to run the gate check independently and report.

options.label: Manual sign-off required
options.text: All phase completions require explicit human 'yes' in a model reply before the status changes to stable.

decision.rationale: Implemented: AGENTS.md constitution + living doc modelReplies + pre-commit hook. AGENTS.md loads at session start (Principle II). Pre-commit hook enforces at commit time (Principle I). tasks.md has per-task constitution checks (Principle VIII). Living doc modelReplies handle human decisions (Principle IX).
